scams.name: Hoi An Tailor Scam & 'Exclusive' Fabric Markup
scams.description: Hoi An's tailor economy is Vietnam's most famous — 300+ tailor shops competing for the suit-and-dress custom of cruise-day and multi-night visitors. Most are legitimate, but a distinct scam ecosystem operates around them. r/VietNam 'Worst Tailor in Hoi An' (comments/1inj004, 2025) is a named 2025 first-person anchor: 'Went to Hoi An to find a good tailor and ended up getting scammed... 90% of tailor-made clothing uses fabric 2-3x cheaper than advertised, with rushed construction and no follow-up fittings. r/VietNam 'Tailor in Hoi an' (comments/1qi7hm7, 2025) documents another 2025 variant with a specific venue warning. The specific scam patterns: (1) 'free tea and design consultation' tout leads tourists to a specific shop where 'partner' commission arrangements inflate prices 30–50%; (2) 'premium fabric' upsell at 3x market rates — fabric that should be $30/metre sold as 'Italian wool' at $90/metre; (3) 'rushed 24-hour delivery' yields low-quality construction that doesn't survive one wash; (4) 'first fitting free, but alterations cost extra' when alterations should be included; (5) hotel-concierge 'partner tailor' that operates a kickback arrangement at the tourist's expense. r/chiangmai 'Did I get scammed, or are they just bad? Tailored suit' (comments/199xbi1) gives the Southeast Asia-wide cross-reference pattern. For older travellers considering a Hoi An tailored piece, the practical playbook: (1) use only community-verified tailors with 4.5+ Google ratings and long review histories — Yaly Couture, Bebe Tailor, and A Dong Silk are the three most-consistently-recommended; (2) allow 2–3 days minimum for a legitimate order (quality construction, 2–3 fittings); (3) bring a reference garment for fit — tailors match it; (4) REFUSE hotel 'partner tailor' recommendations; (5) verify fabric composition by touch and burn-test before purchase; (6) expect $150–$250 for a quality suit, $80–$150 for a tailored dress; $40 for a 'cheap shirt' is likely a scam; (7) pay 50% deposit, 50% on final fitting — NEVER pay 100% upfront; (8) for older travellers, skip the 1-day cruise-excursion rush entirely — tailoring needs time.
scams.avoidance: Use community-verified tailors: Yaly Couture, Bebe Tailor, A Dong Silk (4.5+ Google ratings) Allow 2–3 days minimum with 2–3 fittings; bring a reference garment for fit matching REFUSE hotel 'partner tailor' recommendations — kickback arrangement Pay 50% deposit, 50% on final fitting — NEVER 100% upfront Expected: $150–$250 suit, $80–$150 dress; below this signals quality issues
scams.location: Hoi An Ancient Town tailor shops (300+ operating), hotel-recommended tailor 'partners,' touts approaching tourists with 'free tea and design' offers, fake 'Worst Tailor' copycat branding

scams.name: Hoi An Lantern Boat Ride Pushy Vendors & Fake Monk
scams.description: Hoi An's iconic lantern-lit river evenings have developed a specific 2025 scam ecosystem. r/VietNam 'Watch out for the Hoi An boat scam' (comments/1hozc4h, 2025) is a named 2025 anchor. r/VietNam 'BEWARE HOI AN SCAM' (comments/1l80zcz, 2025) is another named 2025 community warning: 'There are some people (we were approached by a middle aged woman) walking around saying th' ey'll help tourists book a boat, then either quote 3–5x the dock rate or funnel the tourist to a boat that charges extra mid-ride for lantern-release fees. r/VietNam 'Scammed in Hoi An' (comments/1c0cwrs, 2025) is another 2025 first-person anchor about the lantern-boat scam: 'lantern boat ride a scam free experience? They're either getting kickbacks from the sc' ammers or actively part of the scheme. The specific variants: (1) mid-aged 'helpful local' approaches offering to 'book a boat'; (2) boat operator quotes low (50K VND) at dock, demands 300K+ at end; (3) lantern-release 'extra fee' 100K VND per lantern mid-ride; (4) 'fake monk' in orange robes at the Japanese Covered Bridge asking for blessings/donations at 100K–500K VND — real monks never solicit. r/VietNam 'Approached by someone doing a tourist survey in Hoi An' (comments/1jf2joj, 2025) documents the English-speaker approach pattern. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) book boat rides ONLY at the posted-price dock (Bach Dang street waterfront) — typical 150K–200K VND for 20–30 minute ride, including 1–2 lanterns; (2) IGNORE 'helpful locals' approaching with boat or tour offers — all are commissioned touts or scammers; (3) at Japanese Covered Bridge, refuse 'blessing' requests from fake monks; real Buddhist monks in Vietnam never solicit money or approach tourists; (4) for lanterns, buy directly from the boat operator (5K–15K VND each) not the mid-river 'release fee' upsell; (5) for older travellers, the daytime Ancient Town walk (10 AM–4 PM) is significantly less scam-pressured than the evening lantern scene.
scams.avoidance: Book boat rides ONLY at posted-price Bach Dang dock (150K–200K VND for 20–30 min) IGNORE all 'helpful locals' approaching with boat or tour offers Refuse 'fake monk' blessing donations — real Buddhist monks never solicit Buy lanterns directly from boat operator (5K–15K VND each) not mid-river upsell Daytime Ancient Town walk (10 AM–4 PM) is less scam-pressured than evening
scams.location: Hoi An Ancient Town Thu Bon River waterfront, Japanese Covered Bridge area, evening lantern-floating booths, women pushing tourists into river-boat rides

scams.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Ticket & 'Fake Ticket Checker' Confusion
scams.description: Hoi An's UNESCO Ancient Town charges a single entry fee that provides access to 5 of 20+ heritage monuments. The ticket policy has generated confusion and a minor scam ecosystem. r/VietNam 'Tickets for old town hoi an' (comments/1hos5u9, 2025) is a 2025 community anchor documenting the May 2023 policy change: 'New fee to enter Hoi An starting May 15' — the 120,000 VND (adult) / 80,000 VND (combined with monuments) ticket is now required for tourists entering the Ancient Town perimeter, not just the monuments themselves. r/VietNam 'Question about Old Town Hoi An' (comments/10t6brp) documents the scope: 'The ticket is to enter the old streets and some special monumental places. The money will' fund heritage preservation. The scam variants that have emerged: (1) unofficial 'ticket checkers' at secondary entry points demanding cash for tickets already purchased; (2) 'combo ticket' touts outside the official booth selling 3x-markup tickets with 'extra access' claims that don't exist; (3) confusion about which monuments your ticket covers (it covers 5 of your choice, not all); (4) entry through back alleys attempted to avoid the fee — but checkers now patrol these routes. r/travel 'Travelling to Hoi An, Vietnam' (comments/1qqx3om, 2025) adds the context about the monthly full-moon festival where street lights are turned off for lantern evenings — the Ancient Town ticket covers this too. For older travellers, the practical playbook: (1) buy Ancient Town tickets at OFFICIAL booths at main entrance points — 120,000 VND adults (2025); the ticket gives access to 5 monuments of your choice from a list of 20+; (2) plan your 5-monument choice: Japanese Covered Bridge, Phung Hung Ancient House, Hai Nan Assembly Hall, Tran Family Chapel, Quan Cong Temple are most community-recommended; (3) keep your ticket visible when walking the Ancient Town — checkers occasionally verify; (4) REFUSE 'ticket checkers' demanding additional cash if you already have a ticket; (5) for older travellers with mobility concerns, the Ancient Town is walkable in 3–4 hours with 2–3 monument stops plus lunch; (6) the 'full moon festival' (monthly, 14th day of lunar month) is free with your Ancient Town ticket — no additional fee.
scams.avoidance: Buy at OFFICIAL booths at main Ancient Town entrance — 120K VND adults (2025) Plan 5-monument choice: Japanese Covered Bridge, Phung Hung, Hai Nan Hall, Tran Family, Quan Cong Keep ticket visible when walking Ancient Town — checkers occasionally verify REFUSE 'ticket checkers' demanding additional cash if you already have a ticket Full-moon festival is FREE with Ancient Town ticket — no additional fee
scams.location: Hoi An Ancient Town entry points (all main-street entries), UNESCO heritage monument access checkpoints, tourist-trap 'ticket-selling' stands outside the legitimate booths

scams.name: Hoi An 'Fruit Ladies' Photo Trap & Forced Weight Overcharge
scams.description: A specific 2025 Hoi An scam targets tourists seeking 'authentic' photos of Vietnamese women carrying bamboo poles with fruit baskets (gánh hàng rong). r/DaNang 'What to scams to look out for in Hoi Ann' (comments/1k18dh6, 2025) documents the named 2025 pattern: 'Not too many scams besides maybe the fruit ladies and you wouldn't expect that but they are aggressive about demanding payment after photos are taken. The scam sequence: (1) a woman in traditional dress with fruit baskets positions herself at a photogenic corner; (2) she offers to let tourists 'try on the hat and baskets for a photo'; (3) once the photo is taken, she demands payment — typically 200K–500K VND, sometimes with 'forced purchase' of fruit at 100K VND for what should cost 10K; (4) if the tourist refuses, she becomes loud and attracts a crowd, escalating social pressure. r/VietNam 'Approached by someone doing a tourist survey in Hoi An' (comments/1jf2joj, 2025) documents the related English-speaker approach pattern: 'After living in Vietnam, if anyone approaches you and speaks English well, it's a scam or' commissioned tout operation. r/VietNam 'Hoi An: a rant' (comments/1mbtpwn, 2025) captures the broader 2025 traveller sentiment: 'Out of all of that Hoi An was our least favourite. Feels like the motto is Cram them in a nd extract every dong.' The fruit-lady scam is part of a broader commercialisation pattern where every photo opportunity has been monetised. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) NEVER accept offers to 'try on' a fruit-basket hat or pose with a stranger's props for a photo; (2) if you want an 'authentic' photo, politely ask from a distance WITHOUT touching props — agree a price (typically 20K–50K VND) before taking the photo; (3) buy fruit ONLY from fixed-stall vendors with posted-price signs, not from mobile fruit-lady carts; (4) typical fruit prices: 20K VND for a pineapple, 30K for 500g rambutan, 40K for a dragon fruit; (5) if caught in a photo-demand, pay 50K VND maximum (already above fair rate) and walk away — scammers rarely escalate beyond shouting; (6) document the experience for r/VietNam community forum so others are warned.
scams.avoidance: NEVER try on a fruit-basket hat or pose with stranger's props For 'authentic' photos, politely ask from a distance WITHOUT touching — agree 20K–50K VND before photo Buy fruit ONLY from fixed-stall vendors with posted prices (20K pineapple, 30K rambutan 500g) If caught in a photo-demand, pay 50K VND maximum and walk away Scammers rarely escalate beyond shouting — don't let crowd pressure coerce you
scams.location: Hoi An Ancient Town streets (Nguyen Thai Hoc, Tran Phu), Hoi An Central Market perimeter, photo-opportunity corners with 'authentic local' women carrying fruit baskets

scams.name: Hoi An Cooking Class / Tour Booking Kickback Fraud
scams.description: Hoi An's cooking-class economy and Cham Island/My Son day-trip bookings have a specific kickback-and-overcharge pattern. r/VietNam 'Scams after scams' (comments/1s5018d, 2025) is a named 2025 anchor documenting the pattern: 'We took tours and attended cooking classes. Totally times... Scam after scam' — kickback-driven recommendations from hotels and touts inflate prices 30–100% above direct-booking rates. r/VietNam 'Hoi An: a rant' (comments/1mbtpwn, 2025) captures the 2025 overcrowding context: 'Out of all of that Hoi An was our least favourite. Feels like the motto is Cram them in' — commercialised tour volume amplifies kickback opportunities. r/VietNam 'I don't get why tourists continue to support these cringy non' (comments/18a9r2s) documents the generic-tour-operator issue that applies in Hoi An. The scam variants: (1) hotel concierge recommends 'partner' cooking class at $50/person when the direct-booking rate at the same venue is $30/person; (2) tout at Ancient Town offers 'discount cooking class' at $35 but it's a lower-quality operator than advertised; (3) 'day trip to My Son temples' quoted at $60 per person via hotel when Klook/GetYourGuide direct is $25; (4) 'Cham Island snorkelling day trip' at $80 via tout when direct is $45; (5) online bookings via unfamiliar aggregators that upcharge 50%. For older travellers considering a Hoi An cooking class or day tour, the protective playbook: (1) book cooking classes directly via the venue's own website — community-recommended: Red Bridge Cooking School (redbridgecookingschool.com), Morning Glory Cooking School (facebook.com/morningglorycooking), Vy's Market Restaurant Cooking Class; expect $25–$40 per person for 4-hour class including market visit; (2) for My Son temples, book via Klook/GetYourGuide at $20–$30 — half-day tour including guide; (3) for Cham Island snorkelling, book via Klook or direct at the An Bang Beach jetty at $40–$55 per person; (4) REFUSE hotel 'partner' recommendations and Ancient Town touts; (5) verify any online booking is via a platform with cancellation protection (Klook, GetYourGuide, Viator) — never wire transfer.
scams.avoidance: Book cooking classes DIRECT: Red Bridge, Morning Glory, Vy's Market ($25–$40/person) For My Son temples, book via Klook/GetYourGuide ($20–$30 half-day) For Cham Island snorkelling, book Klook or An Bang jetty direct ($40–$55) REFUSE hotel 'partner' recommendations and Ancient Town touts Only use platforms with cancellation protection (Klook, GetYourGuide, Viator) — never wire transfer
scams.location: Hotel-concierge 'partner' cooking class and tour bookings, Hoi An Ancient Town tout-driven bookings, online bookings via unfamiliar aggregators

scams.name: Hoi An Beach Bicycle & Motorbike Rental Damage Claims
scams.description: Hoi An's bike-rental economy serves the daily commute to An Bang Beach (5 km east of Ancient Town). The scam: rental shops take a 'deposit' (cash, passport, or both) and at return claim minor scratches or tyre issues to retain the deposit. r/VietNam 'The scams in Vietnam are exhausting' (comments/1gdv5o1, 2025) captures the broader 2025 pattern: 'In future drive off or buy/rent a stronger bike than police. I' — the rental + police shakedown combination is documented. The scam variants: (1) bicycle rental shop takes 200K VND deposit, claims 'scratch damage' at return demanding 150K+ VND; (2) passport taken as deposit and withheld until additional 'cleaning fee' is paid; (3) motorbike rental at $5–$10/day shop claims 'helmet damage' or 'fuel shortage' at return; (4) hotel-provided 'free bicycles' charged 300K+ VND at checkout for 'damage' that wasn't documented. r/travel 'Don't fall for this scam if you're travelling to Thailand' (comments/1ga4wy3) gives the Southeast Asia-wide passport-deposit warning: 'It's not a scam. Every time we travel to the islands in Thailand they take passports as deposit — but the cross-Asia concern about passport-retention is real in Hoi An too. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) use hotel-provided bicycles where possible — most 3-4 star Hoi An hotels include bikes free with the stay; (2) if renting independently, use established operators (Mr. Hai, The Pedal Collective, Long Life Bikes) with clear written policies; (3) NEVER leave your passport as a deposit — offer cash deposit only (200K VND is standard); (4) photograph the bike from all angles BEFORE riding away; (5) for motorbikes, only use Motorvina/Tigit-quality operators with English paperwork; (6) at return, video the bike/motorbike showing no new damage; (7) if the shop claims damage you didn't cause, dispute with photographic evidence and contact Hoi An Tourist Police (Hoang Dieu Street, +84 235 3861 234) if escalated.
scams.avoidance: Use hotel-provided bicycles where possible (most 3-4 star Hoi An hotels include them) For independent rental, use Mr. Hai, The Pedal Collective, or Long Life Bikes NEVER leave passport as deposit — cash deposit 200K VND is standard Photograph bike from all angles BEFORE riding away At return, video the bike showing no new damage
scams.location: Hoi An An Bang Beach bicycle rental shops, hotel-rental bicycles with 'damage deposit' at return, motorbike rentals at $5–$10/day operators
